title: The Strict Out-of-Bounds Exception (Java Substring Defect)
pattern: A string or collection slicing/sub-ranging API throws a checked error or returns an `Err` variant if the requested indices exceed the collection boundaries.
why_bad: It forces the caller to write 5–10 lines of boundary-clamping code to avoid a crash or error, turning a simple one-line extraction into a source of potential bugs. Defining a partial range should naturally yield the intersection of the requested range and the actual range.
detection: Slicing APIs returning error types on out-of-range parameters instead of clamping indices to valid bounds.
fix: Modify the API to clamp boundaries automatically, returning all available overlapping characters (similar to Python list slicing), defining the boundary exception out of existence.
source: John Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 10.5 ("Example: Java substring method").
